whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Marketing Cloud Advanced Cross-Channel AP exam?

personas.label: Cross-channel marketers
personas.description: You plan campaigns that use email, SMS, push, and advertising and want to validate your orchestration skills.

personas.label: Marketing Cloud implementation consultants
personas.description: You deliver cross-channel Marketing Cloud solutions for clients.

personas.label: Advanced Journey Builder users
personas.description: You build branching journeys and use Einstein tools to coordinate customer engagement.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Marketing Cloud Advanced Cross-Channel exam?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam extends beyond email marketing. It covers advanced Journey Builder features, Mobile Studio, Advertising Studio, and Einstein engagement tools. Email Studio experience alone may not cover the required cross-channel skills.
bullets: 40 scored questions in 60 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
67% to pass, which is 27 correct answers out of 40.
Cross-channel practice. Review SMS, push, audience synchronization, and multichannel journeys.
Einstein features. Study Engagement Scoring, Send Time Optimization, and Content Selection.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build multi-channel journeys that use SMS and push along with email. Practise setting up advertising audiences and Einstein engagement splits before booking.

examFormat.heading: Marketing Cloud Advanced Cross-Channel exam format
examFormat.intro: The proctored exam is offered online or at a test centre. Many items describe a multichannel marketing scenario.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios may ask you to plan a cross-channel journey, select an Einstein feature for personalization, or meet mobile messaging consent requirements.
bestWayToPass: Use advanced Journey Builder tools: Review Einstein Engagement Splits, Random Splits, Wait Until Event, and Engagement Frequency Splits.
Know mobile consent: Study SMS opt-in requirements, push permissions, and how consent differs by channel.
Study Advertising Studio audiences: Learn how audiences sync to ad platforms and how lead forms return data.
Apply Einstein engagement tools: Understand how scoring, send-time optimization, and content selection support personalization.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers advanced cross-channel marketing in Marketing Cloud Engagement, including Journey Builder, MobileConnect, MobilePush, Advertising Studio, Contact Builder, and Einstein engagement tools. Check the current exam guide for the exam’s question count, time, and passing score.

keyConcepts.h2: Marketing Cloud Advanced Cross-Channel: key topics

blocks.heading: Advanced Journey Builder
blocks.body: Advanced Journey Builder includes Einstein Engagement Splits that route based on engagement scores, Random Splits for experiments, Engagement Frequency Splits based on recent messaging volume, and Wait Until Event activities. Consider how the contact enters, how the journey coordinates with other journeys, and whether contacts can re-enter. Be ready to choose the split that matches the requirement.

blocks.heading: MobileConnect and MobilePush
blocks.body: MobileConnect supports SMS and MMS marketing, including keywords, short codes, and API-triggered sends. MobilePush sends notifications to registered iOS and Android apps and can support in-app messages. Both can be used as Journey Builder activities. Learn channel-specific consent: SMS requires explicit opt-in, including under TCPA in the United States; push messages require app-level permission. Do not treat email consent as consent for mobile channels.

blocks.heading: Advertising Studio audience activation
blocks.body: Advertising Studio can sync Marketing Cloud audiences to advertising platforms such as Facebook Custom Audiences and Google Customer Match. Lead Ads can send captured lead information back to Marketing Cloud data extensions. Audience Builder supports audience creation across data sources. Know how marketers activate and suppress audiences and where the data moves.

blocks.heading: Contact Builder and identity
blocks.body: Contact Builder links data extensions to contact records through attribute groups and key fields, commonly Subscriber Key. Data Designer defines the contact model and relationships. A unified contact identity allows email, SMS, push, and advertising data to refer to the same person. Use consistent keys to avoid duplicate profiles and disjointed communications.

blocks.heading: Einstein engagement tools
blocks.body: Einstein Engagement Scoring estimates a contact’s likelihood to open, click, convert, or unsubscribe. Scores are refreshed and can support segmentation and personalization. Send Time Optimization selects an email delivery time based on a contact’s history. Einstein Content Selection chooses content based on predicted engagement. Match the feature to the personalization or timing goal and understand what data it needs.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Marketing Cloud Advanced Cross-Channel AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: Practise coordinating channels in Marketing Cloud, using advanced Journey Builder options, and applying personalization tools to a clear business need.

blocks.heading: Build advanced journeys
blocks.body: Review entry sources, journey activities, Einstein splits, and Random Splits. Know how re-entry and frequency limits affect contacts.

blocks.heading: Coordinate channels
blocks.body: Plan how email, SMS, push, and advertising work together. Consider contact preferences, consent, frequency, and suppression.

blocks.heading: Separate marketing from transactional messages
blocks.body: Review how consent and transactional send definitions apply, including messages initiated through APIs.

blocks.heading: Personalize at scale
blocks.body: Use data extension lookups and AMPscript for conditional content. Understand when Einstein Content Selection fits.

blocks.heading: Measure and improve journeys
blocks.body: Review journey analytics, control groups, and frequency tools to measure paths and optimize message cadence.

sampleQuestions.question: A journey should send SMS only to contacts who did not open an email three days earlier. Which tool should route them?
options: A decision split using stored profile data
A separate journey launched manually
A suppression list for email openers
An engagement split on the email
sampleQuestions.explanation: An engagement split checks whether a contact opened or clicked an earlier journey message.
whyWrong: Decision splits evaluate stored data, not activity on the email.
A manual journey is disconnected from the earlier send and its results.
A suppression list excludes contacts rather than routing them along a journey.

sampleQuestions.question: What is needed before a journey can send a contact an SMS?
options: A purchase within the last year
Membership in an email publication list
A mobile number and recorded SMS consent
A confirmed email address
sampleQuestions.explanation: SMS messaging requires a usable phone number and opt-in; email permission is separate.
whyWrong: Purchase history is not required to send a message.
Publication lists manage email preferences.
Email deliverability does not determine SMS eligibility.

sampleQuestions.question: Why use one contact key across channels?
options: It sets the journey wait time
It connects the same person’s channel records
It determines the order of journey activities
It selects the sending business unit
sampleQuestions.explanation: A shared contact key links the person’s email, mobile, push, and other channel records.
whyWrong: Wait and time-zone behavior use separate settings.
The canvas defines activity order.
Business unit access is configured separately.

sampleQuestions.question: A message should be sent at 9 a.m. in each contact’s local time. What feature should be used?
options: Route by the contact’s country
Use activity send-time and time-zone settings
Wait a fixed number of hours
Build one journey for each time zone
sampleQuestions.explanation: Journey timing settings can send at a specified local time rather than after one fixed delay.
whyWrong: Country routing alone does not set the delivery time.
A fixed wait can end at different local times.
Separate journeys for every time zone duplicate the logic.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a push notification deep link do?
options: Confirms delivery to Marketing Cloud
Opens a relevant screen inside the app
Sets how long the notification remains visible
Records the user’s permission for future messages
sampleQuestions.explanation: A deep link directs the user to a specific place in the app.
whyWrong: Delivery status is reported separately.
Display duration is controlled by the device and operating system.
Consent is handled through app permission and related settings.

sampleQuestions.question: A campaign uses email, SMS, and push. What risk should the team manage?
options: Sending too many messages to the same person
Being unable to reuse one creative format across channels
Being unable to report on multiple channels
Needing a separate Marketing Cloud account per channel
sampleQuestions.explanation: The same contact may be reachable through all three channels, so frequency controls and suppression help prevent over-messaging.
whyWrong: Different channels may need different creative formats.
Marketing Cloud supports cross-channel reporting.
Multiple channels can be managed within an account.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the journey entry-source re-evaluation frequency control?
options: How long the journey stays active
Which channels may be used
How many times a contact may re-enter
How often new eligible contacts are added
sampleQuestions.explanation: Re-evaluation frequency determines how often the entry source is checked for new qualifying contacts.
whyWrong: Journey duration is not controlled by entry-source frequency.
Journey activities determine channel use.
Re-entry behavior is configured separately.

sampleQuestions.question: A contact replies STOP to an SMS. What should happen?
options: Opt the contact out of SMS promptly
Remove the contact from every channel and journey
Unsubscribe the contact from email as well
Wait for an agent to approve the opt-out
sampleQuestions.explanation: STOP is a mobile opt-out keyword and the SMS opt-out should take effect promptly.
whyWrong: An SMS opt-out does not automatically remove consent for every channel.
Email consent is separate from SMS consent.
Requiring manual approval would delay a required opt-out.

sampleQuestions.question: Why use a holdout group in a cross-channel program?
options: Test whether creative renders on devices
Ensure some people never receive marketing
Reduce the amount of data processed
Measure the program’s incremental effect
sampleQuestions.explanation: A holdout provides a comparison group to show what would have happened without the program.
whyWrong: Rendering is checked with previews and test sends.
Consent controls determine whether a person may receive marketing.
Reducing processing is not the purpose of a holdout.

sampleQuestions.question: How does an API event entry source differ from a data extension entry source?
options: API events are real time; data extension entries are scheduled
API events support email only; data extensions support mobile only
Only data extensions require configuration
API events work only in sandboxes
sampleQuestions.explanation: An external system can send an API event to enter a contact promptly, while a data extension source is evaluated on a schedule.
whyWrong: Both entry sources can support journeys with different channels.
Both require configuration, though the setup differs.
Both can be used in different environments.

sampleQuestions.question: A live journey needs a subject-line change. What should the marketer do?
options: Edit the email directly and let the journey pick it up
Pause the journey and edit the running version
Create a new journey version
Duplicate the journey and run both
sampleQuestions.explanation: Running journey versions are locked; make the change in a new version.
whyWrong: The active journey references the version of the activity it started with.
Pausing does not make the version editable.
Parallel journeys may cause duplicate messages.

sampleQuestions.question: How can the team measure whether adding SMS improved an email program?
options: Review SMS click-through rate alone
Compare incremental conversions
Count the total number of texts delivered
Count how many email sends were removed
sampleQuestions.explanation: A comparable group helps measure conversions attributable to the added channel.
whyWrong: SMS clicks alone do not show what would have happened without SMS.
Delivered volume is activity, not incremental value.
Reducing email sends does not show whether outcomes improved.

sampleQuestions.question: What should guide the channel selected for a message?
options: Urgency, consent, and user preference
The channel the marketing team finds easiest
The highest open rate from last quarter
The lowest cost per message
sampleQuestions.explanation: Choose a channel that suits the message and the contact’s permissions and engagement.
whyWrong: Internal convenience does not center the customer need.
Past open rates may not predict response to this message.
Cost alone ignores consent and suitability.

sampleQuestions.question: A contact reaches the journey but never arrives at an SMS activity. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the contact has a recent purchase
Whether the account has enough send capacity
Whether a split sent the contact down another path
Whether the email has a working deep link
sampleQuestions.explanation: Journey splits can route contacts away from an activity, so inspect the contact’s path first.
whyWrong: Purchase history matters only if it is part of a decision rule.
Capacity limits would affect sending rather than journey routing.
Deep links control the destination after a push tap, not journey entry to SMS.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the goal of cross-channel orchestration?
options: Send the same message on every channel at once
Let each channel team run independent campaigns
Coordinate the customer conversation
Replace email with mobile and push
sampleQuestions.explanation: Cross-channel orchestration coordinates channels so each message supports a coherent customer experience.
whyWrong: Duplicate messages across channels can overwhelm contacts.
Separate campaigns can conflict or repeat messages.
Channels can complement one another rather than replace email.
